title: Keeping the Heat Moving: How a Data Centre Stays Cool

devices.what: the building section sheet of the example data hall, drafted once and held, parts changing state on the spoken word
flows as moving parts: cool air as narrow line arrows, heat as amber wavy marks, water as marks travelling along the pipes
a DETAIL view below the sheet reached by a camera move down: CRAH coil, inlet band, chiller circuit; the fridge as its own sheet
the chain of links lettered along the foot of the sheet: four outlined in b04, seven lit one by one in b18, recalled in b26
N plus one as a counted row: units bracketed N plus one dashed spare; running, failed (coral), standby (dashed) states
join material: a camera move over the drawing, down into a detail and back up; a cut only to the fridge and at the failure chapter

value_script.why: a quiet hall: the sheet nearly empty
the sheet fills link by link
the failure chapter: flows dimmed, coral on the failed unit
the lift at the close: every flow running, mint spares

parts.what: the data hall in building section on station 'section' (zone about x 120 to 1220, y 240 to 800): a raised floor plenum (y about 720 to 800) with perforated tiles in front of the racks, two rack rows in section whose fronts face a shared cold aisle in the middle and whose backs face hot aisles at either side, the hall ceiling as a return path. Each rack shows a few server slots. States: still (outlines only), running (slots lit faintly), throttled (slots dimmed, for b22), contained (doors and roof panels closed over the cold aisle, for b12 on). API exposes named anchor points (each rack front and back, the cold aisle, both hot aisles, the tiles, the ceiling return run, the floor plenum run) so flows are drawn by beats onto the same geometry. Supports drawing on in drafting order and placing already drafted (for beats that return to the sheet after a camera move).

three CRAH cabinets standing at the hall's left edge (tall outlined cabinets, a fan disc in each that can turn, a coil drawn as a zigzag inside), labelled crah 1, crah 2, crah 3. Per unit states: running (fan turning, ink outline), failed (fan stopped, coral outline), standby (dashed hidden outline, fan still), starting (fan spinning up to running, outline turning solid with a mint tick). Default: units 1 and 2 running, unit 3 standby. A bracket helper that marks units 1 and 2 as N and unit 3 as spare.

the chilled water loop: a supply pipe and a return pipe from the CRAH coils down and across to the plant room (zone about x 1300 to 1820, y 420 to 800), two pumps side by side on the loop (pump a duty, pump b standby) each with an impeller that turns, a buffer tank on the loop, and the chiller as an outlined box the loop passes through, a riser from the chiller up to the roof. Pump states: running (impeller turning), stopped (coral outline, impeller still), standby (dashed), starting. Buffer tank state: a level (full, draining slowly). Water flow marks travel along the pipes in the loop direction at a set speed; return water drawn as warm (amber tint on the marks), supply water cool (line tone). Placeable already drafted.

the heat rejection unit on the roof above the plant room (zone about x 1380 to 1780, y 110 to 260): an outlined cooler with a fan on top, labelled cooling tower or dry cooler; heat marks lift off it into the sky. States: idle, running (fan turning, heat lifting).

the lesson's shared flow vocabulary, so every beat draws air, heat and water alike: airArrow along a polyline (narrow line tone arrow, travelling dashes while it runs), heatMarks (amber wavy marks rising from a region, gathering under a ceiling when told), warmAir (amber arrows), a colour change along a path from cool line tone to amber for air passing through racks. Start, run and stop on given times; a stopped flow fades; nothing parks on a label.

the chain of links along the foot of the sheet (y about 840 to 920, full safe width): link cards joined by short connectors, lettered lower case mono. States: outlined (faint), lit (ink), active (cyan highlight on one link). It can hold four links (server, air, water, outdoors) or seven (server, air, air handler, water, pump, chiller, outdoors), growing from four to seven in place.

a small monitoring panel drawn as an outlined screen part with mono rows (crah 1, crah 2, crah 3, pump a, pump b), each row with a status mark; a row can raise an alarm (coral mark and the word alarm) and a leader can point from the panel to the unit on the sheet. Sits in free sheet space above the hall (about x 520 to 980, y 100 to 230).
a hall temperature readout as a narrow thermometer gauge with NO numbers: a column that can rise (amber) from a normal mark toward a warning line, and fall back. Sits beside the hall near the racks.
